# Draft:Jason Kyle Howard

----
Jason Kyle Howard is a political journalist and culture writer, and serves as Senior Ideas Editor for Salon.com.
Early life and education
Howard was born in Pineville, Kentucky, and graduated from The George Washington University with a BA in Political Communication in 2003. He holds an MA in history from the University of Kentucky and an MFA in Writing from Vermont College of Fine Arts.
Writing & Editing Career
From 2004 to 2005, Howard served as senior editor and staff writer for Equal Justice Magazine, a national quarterly published by Legal Services Corporation.
His first book, ''Something's Rising: Appalachians Fighting Mountaintop Removal, was published in 2009 by the University Press of Kentucky. Co-written with bestselling novelist Silas House, it examines the controversial practice of mountaintop removal coal mining through the lives of thirteen activists including folk singer Jean Ritchie, country music singer Kathy Mattea, bestselling novelist and former West Virginia gubernatorial candidate Denise Giardina, 2003 Goldman Environmental Prize winner Julia "Judy" Bonds, and others. Something's Rising'' was called "a revelatory work" by the historian Studs Terkel and received praise from Publishers Weekly, Booklist, the Washington Times, and other media outlets.
Howard's follow-up, A Few Honest Words: The Kentucky Roots of Popular Music, was released in 2012 by the University Press of Kentucky and explores how Kentucky's culture, geography, history, and storytelling traditions have influenced American music through the work of musicians including Naomi Judd, Joan Osborne, Dwight Yoakam, Nappy Roots, Matraca Berg, Jim James, and other songwriters and musicians.
Howard's writing has been featured in New York Times, The Atlantic, POLITICO Magazine, The New Republic, Washington Monthly, Oxford American, Town & Country, Garden & Gun, Sojourners, and numerous other publications.
From 2013 to 2025 Howard served as editor of Appalachian Review, formerly Appalachian Heritage, a literary quarterly based at Berea College.
In 2025 he became Senior Ideas Editor for Salon.com, where he writes about the Democratic Party's efforts to construct a winning message and agenda, and how politicians use political rhetoric to influence public opinion and shape the American people's perception of political and cultural moments.
Academic Career
Howard has taught at Berea College since 2013. He also serves on the faculty of Spalding University's Naslund-Mann Graduate School of Writing.
Personal Life
Howard is a gay man who has written about LGBTQ life in America and the South. He is married to the novelist Silas House.
